idiom_name: exported toDto / fromDto functions typed on both shapes
implementation_notes: TypeScript's idiom is a module of pure functions typed on both sides - `export const toDto = (u: User): UserDto => ({ id: u.id, name: u.fullName })` - which gives an in-one-place translation the compiler checks field by field, so an added field on either type is an error at the mapper and nowhere else. Keep the module importing both shapes and neither shape importing the mapper; declare the boundary DTO as a `type`/`interface` (or generate it from the API schema) and pin literal unions with `as const` or string-literal types. The types are erased at runtime, so these mappers must not stand at a trust boundary: use the schema variant when the input is untrusted, and keep plain functions for internal hand-offs where the data is already typed.
pitfalls: A return-type annotation catches missing fields, but an `as UserDto` cast or an `any` parameter disables that check exactly where the boundary is weakest.
`exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and `strictNullChecks` change what `d.name ?? fallback` means: without them, an explicitly undefined field and an absent one are treated alike.
Interface-to-interface assignment is structural: a DTO with a superset of fields passes as the domain shape, so the mapper can silently forward internal fields unless the target type is closed.

variants.name: Schema-first boundary mapping with zod
variants.idiom_name: z.object(...) schema with parse / safeParse and a transform to the domain value
variants.implementation_notes: At a trust boundary the mapper should validate while it translates: declare a `z.object({...})` that mirrors the wire shape, call `Schema.parse(payload)` (or `safeParse` for a typed error path) and chain `.transform(...)` to produce the domain value, so one declaration owns names, types, defaults and the conversion. `z.infer<typeof Schema>` removes the duplicate DTO interface, and `strict()`/`strip()` state explicitly what happens to unknown keys. Choose it for request bodies, message payloads and third-party APIs; keep the plain typed mappers for internal boundaries where the data is already typed and parsing would only add cost.
pitfalls: `.default(false)` turns a missing key into false; if 'absent' must stay distinguishable, model it as `.optional()` and decide in the transform.
`.transform()` runs only after validation and its errors are no longer zod errors, so domain failures need their own error type at the call site.
Schemas and TypeScript interfaces drift when both are maintained: infer the type from the schema or generate one from the other, never both by hand.
